title: Ted
summary: Ted is a 2012 American comedy, the first feature film directed by Seth MacFarlane, the creator of Family Guy, who also co-wrote it and gives the title character his voice and his movements through motion capture. On Christmas Day in 1985, a lonely eight-year-old in Norwood, Massachusetts, wishes that his new teddy bear could come to life and be his friend, and the wish comes true. Twenty-seven years later, John Bennett (Mark Wahlberg) still shares a Boston apartment with Ted, now a crude, hard-partying bear, and with his girlfriend Lori (Mila Kunis), who wants John to grow up. When Ted moves into a place of his own, the pull between the old friendship and the relationship nearly costs John both, until an obsessed fan kidnaps Ted and the three must come together. The film is rated R for crude and sexual content, constant strong language and drug use. It was the highest-grossing comedy of 2012, its opening song was nominated for an Academy Award, and its sequel, Ted 2, followed in 2015.

pieces.name: Boston
pieces.sentence: John, Lori and Ted live in Boston, and the film was shot across the city, from South End streets to the Charles River Esplanade and Fenway Park.
pieces.about: Boston, officially the City of Boston, is the capital and most populous city in the Commonwealth of Massachusetts in the United States. The city serves as the cultural and financial center of the New England region of the Northeastern United States. It has an area of 48.4 sq mi (125 km2) and a population of 675,647 as of the 2020 census, making it the third-largest city in the Northeast after New York City and Philadelphia. The Greater Boston metropolitan statistical area, including and surrounding the city, is the largest in New England and eleventh-largest in the country.

pieces.name: Christmas
pieces.sentence: On Christmas Day 1985, young John wishes that his new teddy bear would come to life and be his friend.
pieces.about: Christmas is an annual festival commemorating the birth of Jesus Christ, observed primarily on December 25 as a religious and cultural celebration among billions of people around the world. A feast central to the liturgical year in Christianity, it follows the season of Advent or the Nativity Fast, and initiates the season of Christmastide, which historically in the West lasts twelve days and culminates on Twelfth Night. Christmas Day is a public holiday in many countries, is celebrated religiously by a majority of Christians, as well as culturally by many non-Christians, and forms an integral part of the holiday season surrounding it.

pieces.name: Wedding
pieces.sentence: John and Lori marry at the end, with Sam J. Jones, the star of Flash Gordon, as the presiding minister.
pieces.about: A wedding is a ceremony in which two people are united in marriage. Wedding traditions and customs vary greatly between cultures, ethnicities, races, religions, denominations, countries, social classes, and sexual orientations. Most wedding ceremonies involve an exchange of marriage vows by a couple; a presentation of a gift ; and a public proclamation of marriage by an authority figure or celebrant. Special wedding garments are often worn, and the ceremony is sometimes followed by a wedding reception. Music, poetry, prayers, or readings from religious texts or literature are also commonly incorporated into the ceremony, as well as superstitious customs.

pieces.sentence: John and Ted's carefree life together includes smoking marijuana, and the film plays it for laughs.
pieces.about: Drugs are substances that alter the functioning of the body and mind when consumed. They can be classified into various categories, including pharmaceutical drugs used for medical purposes, recreational drugs taken for pleasure or euphoria, and illicit drugs that are prohibited by law. Drugs can have both beneficial and harmful effects on individuals, depending on factors such as dosage, frequency of use, and individual characteristics.

pieces.name: Kidnap
pieces.sentence: Donny kidnaps Ted to be his son's toy; Ted manages to phone John before he is caught again, and John and Lori track Donny down.
pieces.about: Kidnapping or abduction is the unlawful abduction and confinement of a person against their will, and is a crime in many jurisdictions. Kidnapping may be accomplished by use of force or fear, or a victim may be enticed into confinement by fraud or deception. Kidnapping is distinguished from false imprisonment by the intentional movement of the victim to a different location.

pieces.about: A marriage proposal is a custom or ritual, common in Western cultures, in which one member of a couple asks the other for their hand in marriage. If accepted, it marks the initiation of engagement, a mutual promise of later marriage.

pieces.name: Friendship and Loyalty
pieces.sentence: John and Ted stay loyal through a breakup, a fight and a kidnapping, and Ted's last wish as his magic fades is for John to be happy with Lori.
pieces.about: Friendship and loyalty are foundational aspects of meaningful relationships. They involve trust, support, and mutual respect, forming the bedrock of strong, enduring connections. Friendship and loyalty are cornerstones of meaningful and lasting relationships. They involve mutual trust, respect, support, and commitment. Cultivating and maintaining these qualities requires effort, open communication, and understanding. Despite the challenges that may arise, the rewards of deep, loyal friendships are immense, providing emotional support, personal growth, and enhanced well-being. By prioritizing these relationships and nurturing them with care, you can enjoy the profound benefits they bring to your life.

Actors bring characters to life by portraying their emotions, thoughts, and actions through their performances. They typically work under the guidance of a director, following scripts or improvising dialogue and actions as required by the role. Actors use various techniques, including voice modulation, body language, and facial expressions, to convey the essence of the characters they portray. Acting often involves a high level of creativity, empathy, and skill in interpreting and embodying different roles.

pieces.sentence: The film's chase ends at Fenway Park, home of the Boston Red Sox; a game there, or at a local ballpark, puts you in the scene.

pieces.name: Relationships
pieces.sentence: Lori has been with John for four years and hopes to marry him, but she feels he cannot move forward while his life still revolves around Ted. After he breaks his word and she ends it, John tries to win her back with a clumsy, heartfelt song in public, and they marry. A person working on a relationship can see that love asks for real change, not only promises.

pieces.name: Maintaining Friendships
pieces.sentence: John and Ted have been best friends since John was eight, but at 35 the friendship is crowding out John's job and his relationship. Ted moves into his own place, and after a serious falling-out the two make up, with the friendship in a new shape. A person can take from it that a long friendship can change as people grow and still last.

pieces.name: Trust and Friendship
pieces.sentence: John tells Lori he is at work when he is really skipping it to be with Ted, and he slips away from her boss's party to Ted's, breaking his word. Ted later admits to Lori his part in John's lapse and offers to step back so she will talk to John again. A viewer sees how small lies wear trust down, and how an honest admission starts to rebuild it.

pieces.name: Ending a Friendship
pieces.sentence: After Lori leaves him, John blames Ted for ruining his life and ends their friendship; their argument turns into a fight, and then they make up. A person thinking about ending a friendship can see the difference between a friendship that has to change and one that has to end, and how anger can make that choice too fast.

pieces.name: Milestone Transitions
pieces.sentence: At 35, John faces the steps of adult life at once: his best friend moves out, his girlfriend hopes for marriage, and in the end he proposes and they marry. A person facing a big change can see how hard it is to leave a comfortable stage of life behind, and that a new stage does not erase the people from the old one.

pieces.name: Independent Living
pieces.sentence: John helps Ted find his own apartment and a job at a grocery store so that Ted can stand on his own, and by the end Ted has comfortably accepted a life of his own. A person moving out for the first time can take from it that a home and work of your own are a step toward a fuller life, not a loss.

pieces.name: Life Balance
pieces.sentence: John's time partying with Ted keeps crowding out his job and his relationship, and he skips work to be with his friend. The film shows what happens when one part of life takes everything: he nearly loses Lori. A person can see the value of giving work, friends and a partner each their own place.

pieces.name: Choices
pieces.sentence: On the night of her boss's party, John has to choose between staying with Lori and meeting Sam J. Jones, the star of his favorite film, at Ted's apartment. He means to stay a few minutes, gets caught up, and Lori breaks up with him. A viewer sees how one small choice can break a promise and change everything that follows.

pieces.name: Peer Pressure
pieces.sentence: Ted lures John away from Lori's work party with the chance to meet Sam J. Jones, and John goes even though he promised to stay. A person feeling pushed by a friend can see how a friend's offer can pull you away from a promise, and that saying no to a friend can be the loyal thing to do.
